debate_title: AI governance frameworks for advanced AI systems

conflicts.point: Whether fixed compute thresholds can effectively separate routine open-source experimentation from dual-use frontier model development without creating enforcement loopholes.

positions.stance: Graduated compute thresholds successfully isolate dangerous dual-use capabilities while exempting smaller open-source developers.
Static compute cutoffs fail because developers can bypass single-model training limits using distributed multi-agent commodity clusters.

verdicts.conflict: Whether fixed compute thresholds can effectively separate routine open-source experimentation from dual-use frontier model development without creating enforcement loopholes.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position rests on documented technical realities regarding distributed computing and parallel processing clusters. Regulators struggle to monitor decentralized hardware pooling, making static compute cutoffs vulnerable to evasion. The safetyist claim relies on administrative assumptions about single-model visibility that ignore modern training techniques.
